title: Natural cohomology-presheaf description of higher direct images on ringed sites
statement:
Work in compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites, and let $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a morphism of sites presented by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $A,B$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, respectively, and $\rho:B\to f_*A$ a morphism of ring sheaves. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $f_*:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ send $M$ to $V\mapsto M(u(V))$, with scalars restricted along $\rho_V$. Assume module sheafification exists [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and both module categories have enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Fix $q\geq0$. For $U\in\mathcal C$, let $H^q_{\mathrm{Mod}(A)}(U,M)$ be the $q$-th right derived functor of additive evaluation $M\mapsto M(U)$ on $A$-module sheaves [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions], with values in abelian groups. For every $A$-module sheaf $M$, these groups form a presheaf of $B$-modules $P^q_M$ on $\mathcal D$, with
$$P^q_M(V)=H^q_{\mathrm{Mod}(A)}(u(V),M).$$
Restrictions are induced by restrictions on an injective resolution; the $B(V)$-action is induced by multiplication through $\rho_V:B(V)\to A(u(V))$ on its evaluated complex. The presheaves $P^q_M$ are functorial in $M$. There is a canonical isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves
$$\sigma_M:(P^q_M)^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qf_*M,$$
where $R^qf_*$ is the right derived functor in the module categories. The isomorphism is induced by the map taking an evaluated resolution cocycle to its cohomology-sheaf section and is natural in $M$: for every $A$-linear morphism $a:M\to M'$, writing $P^q(a)$ for the induced presheaf map,
$$R^qf_*(a)\circ\sigma_M=\sigma_{M'}\circ(P^q(a))^\#.$$
No flatness of $\rho$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images, statement and proof, lines 746–785: explicitly for a morphism of ringed sites and module sheaves. Naturality is the cocycle-to-cohomology-sheaf construction in that proof.

proof.text: Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ using lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero (1), and put $K^\bullet=f_*I^\bullet$. The module-category description of kernels shows that evaluation and $f_*$ preserve kernels: evaluate the kernel at $U$ or at $u(V)$, respectively; restriction of scalars changes neither that kernel nor the additive operations. Both functors are additive and left exact. The resolution-computation isomorphisms of lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift give $H^q_{\mathrm{Mod}(A)}(u(V),M)\cong H^q(I^\bullet(u(V)))$ and $R^qf_*M\cong\mathcal H^q(K^\bullet)$, the latter in $B$-module sheaves. Write $L^\bullet$ for the underlying complex of presheaves of $B$-modules of $K^\bullet$, and $Q^q=\ker(d_L^q)/\operatorname{im}(d_L^{q-1})$ in that presheaf category. For $q=0$ use $L^{-1}=0$.

Kernels and cokernels of presheaves of $B$-modules are formed objectwise: take the module kernel or quotient at each object and use the induced semilinear restrictions; the objectwise universal properties give the presheaf universal properties. Thus $Q^q(V)=\ker(d_I^q(u(V)))/\operatorname{im}(d_I^{q-1}(u(V)))$, with scalar action $b[z]=[\rho_V(b)z]$. The differentials are $A$-linear, so this action is well defined. For $v:V'\to V$, naturality of $\rho$ and semilinearity of restriction give $(b[z])|_{V'}=b|_{V'}[z|_{u(V')}]$. Identity and composition of restrictions hold already on $I^\bullet$. This identifies $Q^q$ with the presheaf $P^q_M$ in the statement, including its specified restrictions and $B$-action, using the computation in step 1.

Apply the exact module-sheafification functor on $(\mathcal D,B)$ from lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact. The natural homology comparison in lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology (c) yields $(Q^q)^\#\cong\mathcal H^q((L^\bullet)^\#)$. Every $L^r$ is the underlying presheaf of the sheaf $K^r$. Its sheafification is canonically $K^r$: by the sheafification universal property the identity of $K^r$ factors through $(L^r)^\#$, and the two composites are identities by uniqueness. The same uniqueness makes these identifications commute with differentials and with complex maps. Therefore $(Q^q)^\#\cong\mathcal H^q(K^\bullet)\cong R^qf_*M$. Define $\sigma_M$ by composing this isomorphism with $(P^q_M)^\#\cong(Q^q)^\#$ from step 2. The cited homology comparison respects cycle inclusions and quotient projections, so its composite with the sheafification unit sends $[z]$ to the cohomology-sheaf section represented by $z$. This is exactly the asserted cocycle map, and all its arrows are $B$-linear.

For $a:M\to M'$, choose resolutions $I,I'$ as above. The statement of lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists supplies an augmentation-preserving $A$-linear complex map $t:I\to I'$ over $a$. For every $V$, lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift applied to evaluation identifies $P^q(a)_V$ with $[z]\mapsto[t^q_{u(V)}(z)]$. This is $B(V)$-linear and commutes with restrictions, since $t$ is a morphism of module-sheaf complexes. Identity and composition hold for these maps because the evaluation right derived functors are functors. Applied to $f_*$, the same cited statement identifies $R^qf_*(a)$ with $\mathcal H^q(f_*t)$ under the resolution-computation isomorphisms. Naturality of the homology comparison from step 3, together with the natural sheafification identifications there, now gives $R^qf_*(a)\circ\sigma_M=\sigma_{M'}\circ(P^q(a))^\#$. Explicitly, both sides precomposed with the presheaf sheafification unit send $[z]$ to the cohomology-sheaf class of $t^q_{u(V)}(z)$; equality after sheafification follows from its universal property.

Finally take $a=\mathrm{id}_M$ in the preceding argument, allowing two different chosen resolutions of $M$. The lift-existence statement again supplies a comparison. The derived-map formula identifies its evaluated cohomology map with the identity of each fixed derived evaluation group, and its direct-image cohomology map with the identity of $R^qf_*M$. Hence the presheaf module structures and $\sigma_M$ agree under the canonical resolution identifications; the construction is canonical. The calculation used only restriction of scalars, linear differentials and exact sheafification. It imposed no flatness condition on $\rho$.

The pushforward and coefficient category agree with 072W: M(u(V)) with scalars restricted along rho, all cohomology computed in Mod(A) and Mod(B). Step 1: resolution existence (degree-zero leaf (1)); evaluation and f_* are left exact because module kernels are sectionwise; iota from derived-map-via-lift, which needs only an additive functor. Step 2, marked elementary: objectwise presheaf kernel/quotient; the B-action through rho is well defined because the differentials are A-linear, and the restrictions are semilinear by naturality of rho. Step 3: exact module sheafification plus exact-functor-homology (c); (L^r)^# = K^r by the universal property; the cocycle compatibility comes from (c). Step 4: lift existence plus the derived-map formula for evaluation and for f_*, then naturality via the uniqueness in the unit's universal property. Step 5: independence of the resolution via h=id. No flatness, no SGA, no homotopy uniqueness assumed. Small cases checked: q=0, a one-object site with Z->Z/2, u=id with q>0, empty covers. No duplicate of the ringed-site module version among the abelian, scheme and ringed-space comparison nodes (lem-sbc-abelian-higher-image-sheafification-functor-iso, lem-pc-cohomology-presheaf-derived-sections-evaluation, lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison, lem-pc-higher-direct-image-coefficient-comparison).
